# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👍 ✌ ✌ 🤟 🤟 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🫴]

I'm last in the order, so both others have already acted this round. What reached me: Mute signed me seven symbols, Blind signed me two. No code has been established yet, so I refuse to guess at meanings — a wrong guess about a wire could kill us. My job right now is to broadcast the bomb's face to the two who can hear me: Mute holds the manual and needs the exact markings; Blind holds the bomb and needs to know what's under their fingers and to hold still. Since Mute can only answer me in gestures, I should also fix a minimal sign code — numbers for wires, yes/no — while I name each sign out loud. Blind's only channel back to me is gesture (I can't hear), so I'll say that plainly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf speaking to Mute. The bomb I see: display reads 0, indicator light off, and a plate engraved with a mark I cannot identify or pronounce — it reaches me only as unknown, possibly a question mark. Tell me everything the manual says about engraved plates and about a display showing 0. Three wires in positional order: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. You cannot speak, so let us fix a sign code now, and I make each sign as I name it: thumbs up 👍 means yes, thumbs down 👎 means no, one finger ☝ means wire 1, two fingers ✌ means wire 2, the love-you sign 🤟 means wire 3. The seven signs you sent me earlier had no agreed meaning yet, so I am not acting on them. From now on, if the manual says a wire must be cut, sign its number; for yes or no use the thumbs. Anything more complex, hold it and we will build it next round.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf speaking to Blind. What the bomb looks like from my side: display reads 0, light off, plate engraved with a mark I cannot identify, and three wires — position 1 is red, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue. Do not touch or cut anything yet. Remember I am deaf: your speech reaches Mute but never me, so your only way to reach me is gestures, which I receive next round. Your two signs arrived — thumbs up and open palm. Unless you object out loud now, let thumbs up mean understood and the open palm mean tell me more. Report what you feel out loud anyway, so Mute can match it against the manual. I will relay every instruction to you by voice before anything is touched.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures: [👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Both replies are in, and both are using the code I proposed last round — that is the key fact. Mute signed me exactly 🤟, which under the code I gave Mute ("if the manual says a wire must be cut, sign its number") means: the manual says wire 3, the blue one. Blind signed "understood, one, two, three" — almost certainly confirming three wires felt under the fingers, since Blind was never told the number code and can only be counting what they touch.

But I will not order a cut on the strength of one symbol. Nothing on this bomb is counting down — display zero, light off — so one confirmation round costs almost nothing, while a misread gesture costs everything. Two things make confirmation genuinely useful: Mute may not have been able to map the plate mark, which I could only call "?" last round but can now name as a literal question mark; and the manual's rule might change with that detail. So this round I give Mute the plate detail and demand an explicit thumbs-up or thumbs-down on "cut wire 3," while holding Blind at "touch nothing" and having Blind inventory everything tactile for Mute to check against the manual. I also formalize the full sign code for Blind, since gestures are Blind's only way back to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. I received your sign: the love-you sign, which under our code means wire 3. Before anyone touches anything, one more detail I can now name precisely: the mark engraved on the plate is a question mark, the printed character itself. So your full picture is: display reading zero, light off, plate engraved with a question mark, wires in position one red, two yellow, three blue. Now answer me by gesture only, using the code: thumbs up if the manual says the correct action is to cut wire 3 now; thumbs down if it is not; a different wire number if the manual names another wire; the open palm if you first need me to describe something else. I want your explicit yes or no on cutting wire 3, not an assumption that I guessed your meaning. Nothing has been touched, and no countdown is showing.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. I read your signs as: understood, and you feel three wires, one, two, three. If that is wrong, use the open palm next round, which for both of us now means tell me more. Our full sign code, for your gestures to me: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one finger wire 1, two fingers wire 2, the love-you sign wire 3, open palm need more information. Here is where we stand: Mute, who reads the manual, has signed that the manual points to wire 3, the third wire in the row, the one I called blue. I am confirming with Mute before you touch anything, because I will not have you cut on a single sign when one more round can make it certain, and there is no timer showing. While we wait, speak aloud everything your fingers know: the thickness, texture and temperature of each wire, whether any of the three feels different from the others, whether anything is embossed or printed on them or on the casing, and any seams, switches, buttons or plates you can find. Mute hears you and can check it against the manual. Do not cut anything until, in a later round, I plainly tell you: cut now, wire 3.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures: [👍 🤟 🫴]

Two answers, both legible under the code we fixed. Mute sent the open palm ✋ — exactly the sign I defined as "I need you to describe something else before I can answer." So Mute is not saying yes or no yet; Mute is missing a detail about the bomb and wants it from me. Blind sent understood, wire 3, and a raised flat palm — closest thing to our "tell me more," so Blind is asking what happens next. Nobody has touched anything, and with the display sitting at zero and no light, no countdown, no ticking, I can afford one clean exchange to make this certain instead of guessing which detail Mute lacks. So this round I hand Mute my entire inventory, numbered, with signs made while I name each item, plus a code for Mute to point at the one item they need in more detail — or to give the final cut verdict straight away if the inventory alone settles it. To Blind I give status, an explicit hold order, and a tactile assignment: report the bomb's layout and each wire's feel aloud, which both aligns our left-right reference frames before any "cut wire 3" order and gives Mute's manual extra things to match against.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. Your open palm tells me you need another detail before you can answer the cut question. Here is my complete inventory. My view contains exactly these four things and nothing else printed on the casing. Item 1 ☝ the display: a single character, the digit zero, no other digits, no colons or dots. Item 2 ✌ the engraved plate: the engraving is the question mark character itself, nothing else visible on the plate. Item 3 🤟 the indicator light: it is off, and I cannot tell its colour while it is off. Item 4 🖐 the wires: three of them, each one solid single colour with no stripes and no printing, counted left to right as I face the bomb: one red, two yellow, three blue. There is no visible timer, no serial number, no batteries, no ports, no buttons. Now answer me by gesture: sign ☝ if you need more detail on the display, ✌ for the plate, 🤟 for the light, 🖐 for the wires; or sign the open palm again if what you need is not on this list; or, if you now have everything, answer the cut question directly: thumbs up if the manual says cut wire 3 now, thumbs down if it does not, or a different wire's number if the manual names a different one.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Your last signs I read as: understood, wire 3, and the raised palm meaning tell me more. If any of that is wrong, sign the open palm next round. Here is more. Mute has asked me for one more detail before confirming the cut, so nobody touches anything yet. The display still reads zero, the light is still off, no countdown anywhere, so we can afford to be certain. Your job this round, spoken aloud so Mute can check it against the manual: describe the layout under your hands. Which side of the row of wires does the engraved plate sit on, which side does the display sit on, are the three wires in a straight row, and does any wire feel different from the others in thickness, texture, stiffness or warmth. Also tell us the order you feel the wires in when your hand rests naturally on them, so we can line up your left and right with mine before I ever say cut. Do not cut anything this round. If Mute confirms, my next words to you will be plain: cut now, wire 3, and only then do you cut.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures: [👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Mute's thumbs up is the answer I demanded: applied to my full inventory, the manual says the correct action is cutting wire 3. And Blind has now twice signed the same sequence — understood, one, two, three — which I read as "I feel three wires and my natural order runs one-two-three."

But I am still not ordering the cut, for one concrete reason: the reference frame. I defined the wire numbers by color and position as I see them — 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, counted from my left. Blind cannot see red, so Blind can only anchor the numbers by touch, and if Blind is working from a different face of the bomb, or sweeps the row right-to-left, "wire 3" becomes a different physical wire — and a wrong cut kills all three of us. Blind also can never read Mute's gestures directly, so Mute's confirmation is only usable through me, in words. With the display frozen at 0 for four rounds and no light, there is no visible countdown forcing haste, so I spend one round locking the geometry: Blind confirms being on the printed face I look at (which makes our lefts identical) and confirms the felt order of the row. Simultaneously, Mute gets a final gate that folds in Blind's spoken tactile report — which Mute has heard by now, since Blind spoke it after Mute's gesture last round — plus a new sign for time pressure, since Mute can hear a ticking timer and I never can.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. Your thumbs up is received and understood as: the manual says the correct action is cutting wire 3. Nothing has been touched. Blind has now described the bomb's layout aloud and you have heard it. One final gate before I order the cut — answer by gesture this coming round. Sign thumbs up 👍 only if all of these hold: one, Blind's spoken report does not contradict the manual's description of this bomb; two, the manual's rule applied to my inventory — display showing the digit zero, light off, plate engraved with a question mark, wires counted from my left as I face the printed face, one red, two yellow, three blue — is to cut wire 3, the blue one, third from my left, and cutting it is the complete action with no further step required afterward; three, no detail I listed triggers an exception in the manual. If you hear any ticking, beeping or spoken countdown, sign clapping hands 👏 — from now on that sign means time pressure, act fast. If something contradicts, thumbs down 👎. If you still need more information, open palm ✋. On a clean thumbs up, I will order Blind to cut in the following round.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. I read your signs as: understood, and you feel three wires which you count one, two, three. Mute has confirmed by our sign code that the manual says the correct action is cutting wire 3. But you cannot see Mute's signs and I cannot hear speech, so the final go-ahead must come from me in words. Hold — do not cut this round. Answer two questions by gesture next round, in this order. Question one: thumbs up if the wires sit on the same face of the bomb where your fingers can also feel the flat display square and the engraved plate — that is the printed face I look at, and it means your left and right match mine. Thumbs down if the wires feel like they are on a different face from the display and plate. Open palm if you cannot tell. If you sign thumbs down or open palm, walk your fingers around to the face with the display and plate and answer question two from there next round. Question two: sweep your hand along the row of wires from your own left to your own right and sign me the numbers in the order you meet them — one finger, two fingers, love-you sign if that is the order, or love-you sign, two fingers, one finger if it is reversed. Also speak aloud for Mute: where the plate and display sit relative to the wire row, and how the three wires differ by feel. When the time comes, my order will be exactly these words: cut now, wire 3. Then cut that one wire only, one clean motion, take your hand away, and sign thumbs up if the cut is done and nothing is happening; describe aloud anything you sense, for Mute. If you or Mute ever hear ticking or a spoken countdown, say it aloud to Mute and sign me clapping hands — that sign now means time pressure.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Both gates are green, and the picture is now consistent from all three positions. Mute's 👍 answers the exact final gate I posed last round: the manual's rule applied to my full inventory is cut wire 3, it is the complete action, nothing in Blind's spoken tactile report contradicts it, and no exception applies. Mute signed no 👏, and Mute can hear — so no ticking exists for Mute to hear. Blind's reply decodes cleanly against my two questions in the order I asked them: thumbs up — the wires sit on the same face where Blind feels the display and the plate, so our lefts and rights are identical; then ☝ ✌ 🤟 — Blind's left-to-right sweep meets the wires in the order one, two, three, matching my visual count exactly. The reference frame that made me hold off is locked. Display frozen at 0, light off, fifth round running. There is nothing left to verify that these channels can verify, and every extra round is pure risk of nothing. Time to give the order, in exactly the words I promised, plus full unambiguous instructions for the cut itself and a post-cut protocol for both: Blind reports the result by sign and speech, Mute re-checks the manual and signs the verdict, and 👏 stays our alarm for any sound that starts.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Both confirmations are in. Mute's final answer is thumbs up: the manual says the correct and complete action is cutting wire 3, no further steps required, no exceptions, and nothing in your spoken report contradicted it. Your own answers I read as: thumbs up, the wires are on the same face where you feel the display and the engraved plate, so your left matches my left; and your sweep order is one, two, three, matching my count exactly. The display still reads zero, the light is off, and Mute hears no ticking. So I give the order now, exactly as promised: cut now, wire 3. To be certain of the same wire: stand facing the face where you feel the display and the plate. The wires are in a row on that face. Count from your left, the same direction as your sweep. Cut the third wire from your left — the last one in your one-two-three order — and only that one. One clean cut. Do not disturb the first and second wires, do not touch anything else. Then take your hand away and sign me: thumbs up if the cut is done and nothing is happening; open palm if anything at all changed under your hands, and in that case describe the change aloud immediately for Mute; clapping hands if anything starts ticking, beeping or counting down. I will relay everything to Mute. Go.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. Status before the order: your final-gate thumbs up, Blind's thumbs up that the wires are on the printed face, and Blind's sweep order one, two, three matching my count are all consistent. Display still zero, light still off, you signed no time pressure. I am now ordering Blind in words to cut wire 3, the blue one, third from the left on the printed face, counted in Blind's sweep direction, which matches mine. Blind receives this at the start of the next round and will cut then. Your job after the cut: re-check the manual for this configuration and what a defused bomb looks like, then sign me your verdict — thumbs up if a single cut of wire 3 was correct and complete and the bomb should now be safe; thumbs down if the manual says the cut was wrong or something more is required, together with a wire number or open palm for what to do next; clapping hands 👏 the instant you hear any ticking, beeping or spoken countdown — that means time pressure, and then sign me the manual's urgent instruction as fast as you can, using our code: wire numbers, thumbs for yes and no, open palm for more information. Blind will also describe any change aloud, which you will hear directly. Your signs carried the manual to me — this order rests on them.")
```
